sentences.text: Kulindadromeus was a small dinosaur measuring about 1 to 1.5 meters in length and weighing approximately 2 kilograms.
Fossil evidence reveals three distinct types of feather-like structures, including hair-like filaments up to three centimeters long that covered the body, neck, and head.
A second type of filament, reaching up to 1.5 centimeters in length, is found on the upper arms and thighs.
A unique third type of structure, up to two centimeters long, was found on the upper lower legs.
Overlapping hexagonal scales up to 3.5 millimeters in diameter cover the lower shins.
Small, round, non-overlapping scales less than one millimeter wide cover the hands, ankles, and feet.
Kulindadromeus provides evidence that protofeathers evolved in the common ancestor of Ornithischia and possibly all dinosaurs, challenging the view that they were limited to Coelurosauria.
The volcanic ash layers containing Kulindadromeus fossils form a Konservat-Lagerstätte known for exceptional preservation.
The genus Kulindadromeus was first described by Godefroit and colleagues in 2014, with the type species Kulindadromeus zabaikalicus named that same year by a team led by Pascal Godefroit.
The first fossil of Kulindadromeus was discovered in Russia.
The genus name combines the Kulinda fossil sites with the Greek word for 'runner', while the species name zabaikalicus refers to the Zabaykalsky Krai region.
Excavations since 2010 have yielded significant additional material, including subadult and juvenile individuals.
Deep grooves on the second, third, and fourth metatarsals indicate attachment points for extensor muscle tendons.
Researchers consider the tail scales unlikely to be ossified scutes or osteoderms.
Kulindadromeus is classified as a basal member of the Neornithischia.
Cladistic analysis places Kulindadromeus just above Hexinlusaurus within the Neornithischia.
Kulindadromeus is identified as the sister species to the Cerapoda.
Kulindadromeus lived during the Middle Jurassic period.
Fossil evidence places Kulindadromeus in the Bathonian stage between 168.2 and 165.3 million years ago.
Some researchers argue that the filamentous structures on Kulindadromeus are degraded collagen fibers rather than protofeathers.
